recent_posts.Post Message: For Cervical Cancer Awareness Month, Sabin is hosting #SocialWithSabin, a social media takeover by partners of the #GlobalHPVConsortium. From CAPED India ⤵️  This #CervicalCancerAwarenessMonth, let’s check the facts. Understanding cervical cancer is the first step to preventing it. The more we know, the better we can protect ourselves. Swipe to learn more and stay informed.  #CAPED

Reaching zero-dose children. Diagnosing missed vaccination opportunities. Engaging schools and communities on the importance of vaccination to help those who need it most.   Fellows in the latest cohort of the COVID-19 Recovery for Routine Immunization Programs Fellowship — supported by Sabin’s Boost Community and the World Health Organization — tackled these lofty goals and more.   Through this fellowship and their membership in Boost, participants made lasting impact in their communities, connected with peers around the world, and learned lessons they will take forward into the rest of their careers.    Hear about their experience, in their own words ⤵

From vaccine development for lethal diseases to rapid global #OutbreakResponse to supporting countries as they improve immunization planning, Sabin celebrates a productive 2025 and looks forward to continued milestones in 2026!   Learn more in these reflections from our leaders, and visit the link in our bio for blogs from CEO Amy Finan, President of Research & Development, Kelly Warfield, and President of Global Immunization Rebecca Martin.

Partners in the #GlobalHPVConsortium work with local organizations every day to #EliminateCervicalCancer and #PreventHPV. Here, @VillageReach takes over our account with #SocialWithSabin as part of #CervicalCancerAwarenessMonth, sharing a success story from #Nigeria ⤵️  --  Enugu https://x.com/sabinvaccine/status/2013673442076250341/photo/1

top_post.post_message: In our January newsletter, dive into our #Marburg outbreak response support in #Ethiopia, #CervicalCancer elimination efforts, our work with hexavalent vaccine adoption, and more.

"Unlike COVID-19, there is no commercial market for a Marburg vaccine. Demand is limited to outbreak response, health workers, and emergency stockpiles. Progress depends almost entirely on public sector and philanthropic investment. Sabin’s role is to ensure that lack of commercial viability does not translate into lack of protection."  Sabin Vaccine Institute CEO Amy Finan reflects on a defining moment in 2025 — when #Ethiopia's Ministry of Health reached out for support as the country faced its first-ever outbreak of #Marburg virus disease.   Having responded to a Marburg outbreak in Rwanda the year before, the Sabin team moved quickly — building on established partnerships and lessons learned to support the national response, while generating evidence to support the development of our investigational cAd3-Marburg vaccine.  Read more ⤵️ https://www.sabin.org/resources/2025-spotlight-reflections-on-outbreak-response-and-generating-meaningful-data/   #OutbreakResponse

board.public_perception_text: Sabin's social media presence continues to strengthen institutional reputation. Our messaging reaches diverse stakeholder groups with strong engagement metrics. Positive sentiment reflects public confidence in our vaccine research and immunization initiatives.
board.donor_engagement_text: Social channels serve as critical touchpoints for demonstrating research impact and organizational effectiveness. Quarterly reports of breakthrough achievements drive stakeholder engagement and support fundraising objectives. Expanding reach indicates growing influence in vaccine policy discussions.
board.risk_management_text: Consistent engagement monitoring identifies potential reputational risks early. Current positioning addresses vaccine concerns and establishes Sabin as trusted authority. Social media serves as early warning system enabling rapid response to misinformation.

assumptions: Reach and impressions are standardized into one visibility metric per platform, using impressions when available and otherwise reach.
Report-facing summary cards use Facebook, Instagram, and LinkedIn only so the dashboard and quarterly report share one scope.
Cross-network post engagements continue to come from Hootsuite's Post engagement aggregate, with X removed when legacy X totals are present.
Detailed platform, program, and post layers continue to use standardized post-level exports where available, and link clicks stay separate from engagement totals.
Owly link-click exports are treated as website-resource traffic enrichment for Facebook and LinkedIn posts; X/Twitter Owly tables are optional when present.
YouTube follower counts remain available in raw Hootsuite exports, but report-facing summary cards exclude YouTube until a matching platform detail layer is maintained.
Actual follower pace uses real January 1 follower counts when they can be recovered from January exports or saved January dashboard artifacts.
Target pace remains a separate benchmark derived from the stated year-end target and annual growth rate.
Monthly export completeness is complete only when the cross-platform aggregate export, all full post-performance exports, and the expected Facebook/LinkedIn Owly website-click exports are present.
Email exports are excluded from social platform calculations to avoid mixing unlike metrics.
Follower pace is labeled slightly behind when actual performance is within 5% of the benchmark pace.

The cross-platform aggregate account_metrics export is the all-platform rollup, and supplemental top-post files may still be needed to support post-level context where full post-performance exports are missing.
